issues.display_title: Issue #178: Implement /health diagnostic endpoint (service & dependency monitoring)
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 09/06/26

✅ Implementation Complete — Ready for Unit Testing

Route :

GET /health

Overview

Implement a comprehensive /health endpoint for the Villume Backend that provides a single diagnostic route to monitor the availability of the core application and its critical third-party dependencies (CockroachDB, Redis, RabbitMQ, Elasticsearch, SMTP).

Design reference: docs/2026-06-10-health-check-design.md

Objective

Enable automated monitoring and manual verification of system health, ensuring all integrated services are reachable and functional.

Scope / Acceptance Criteria

  • GET /health route registered in cmd/api/main.go (unauthenticated).
  • Service probes implemented:
    • Database (CockroachDB) via GORM sql.DB.Ping()
    • Redis via redis.Client.Ping()
    • RabbitMQ — verify global rabbitmq.Conn initialized and not closed
    • Elasticsearch — new Ping() in src/lib/elastic/elastic.go (lightweight HTTP GET)
    • SMTP — new PingSMTP() in src/lib/mailer/mailer.go (TCP dial, 2s timeout)
  • Health controller CheckHealth in src/controllers/healthController.go aggregates probe results.
  • Status aggregation logic:
    • ok — all services up
    • degraded — a non-critical service (Redis, RabbitMQ, Elasticsearch, SMTP) is down
    • error — primary Database is down
  • HTTP status codes:
    • 200 OK — healthy or degraded (still functional)
    • 503 Service Unavailable — Database down (cannot function)
  • Structured JSON response.

Expected response format

{
  "status": "ok",
  "services": {
    "database": "up",
    "redis": "up",
    "rabbitmq": "up",
    "elasticsearch": "up",
    "smtp": "up"
  }
}

Testing Scenarios (for Tester)

Use these scenarios to validate the /health endpoint. For each, record the observed status field, the HTTP status code, and the per-service states.

TC-1 — Happy Path (all services up)

  • Pre-condition: Database, Redis, RabbitMQ, Elasticsearch, and SMTP are all running and reachable.
  • Steps: Send GET /health.
  • Expected:
    • HTTP 200 OK
    • "status": "ok"
    • Every entry in services is "up".

TC-2 — Degraded: SMTP down

  • Pre-condition: All services up except SMTP (stop the mail server or block its port).
  • Steps: Send GET /health.
  • Expected:
    • HTTP 200 OK (system still functional)
    • "status": "degraded"
    • services.smtp = "down", all others "up".
    • SMTP probe should time out within ~2 seconds (no long hang).

TC-3 — Degraded: Redis down

  • Pre-condition: All services up except Redis.
  • Steps: Send GET /health.
  • Expected:
    • HTTP 200 OK
    • "status": "degraded"
    • services.redis = "down".

TC-4 — Degraded: RabbitMQ down

  • Pre-condition: All services up except RabbitMQ (stop broker / close connection).
  • Steps: Send GET /health.
  • Expected:
    • HTTP 200 OK
    • "status": "degraded"
    • services.rabbitmq = "down".

TC-5 — Degraded: Elasticsearch down

  • Pre-condition: All services up except Elasticsearch.
  • Steps: Send GET /health.
  • Expected:
    • HTTP 200 OK
    • "status": "degraded"
    • services.elasticsearch = "down".

TC-6 — Critical Failure: Database down

  • Pre-condition: Stop / disconnect CockroachDB.
  • Steps: Send GET /health.
  • Expected:
    • HTTP 503 Service Unavailable
    • "status": "error"
    • services.database = "down".

TC-7 — Multiple non-critical services down

  • Pre-condition: Redis AND SMTP both down, Database up.
  • Steps: Send GET /health.
  • Expected:
    • HTTP 200 OK
    • "status": "degraded"
    • Both services.redis and services.smtp = "down".

TC-8 — Database down + others down (priority of status)

  • Pre-condition: Database down and at least one non-critical service down.
  • Steps: Send GET /health.
  • Expected:
    • HTTP 503 Service Unavailable
    • "status": "error" (database failure takes precedence over degraded).

TC-9 — No authentication required

  • Pre-condition: All services up.
  • Steps: Call GET /health without any auth token / header.
  • Expected: HTTP 200 OK returned — endpoint is publicly reachable for monitoring tools.

TC-10 — Response contract & performance

  • Steps: Call GET /health repeatedly.
  • Expected:
    • Response is valid JSON matching the documented schema (keys: status, services with all 5 services present).
    • Content-Type: application/json.
    • Endpoint responds promptly even when a probe fails (slow/unreachable service must not hang the whole response beyond the configured timeout, ~2s for SMTP).

Notes for QA: Suggested tools — curl, Postman, or a monitoring agent. To simulate "down" states, stop the relevant container/service or block its port via firewall rules. Verify the HTTP status code AND the JSON status field together, as they are intended to be consistent.
